main_text.p: fior:cholagogis, si biliosus est, phlegmagogis, si pituitosus. Si doleant, anodynis saepe diētis: vt, lacte cocto, vitellis ouorum, oesypo, butyro recenti dolor est placandus. Si haemorrhoides sint occultae, & tumore doleat, anodynis placetur, vel sanguis emittatur his apertis per hirudines, aut scalpellum, aut anastomotica post dicenda. Si vero nec tumor est ingens, nec dolor, naturae permitte: nec aperi, nisi tumoris, aut doloris magnitudo compellat: quod saepe cancri, fistulae, & affectus alij difficiles, his partibus per valentia remedia apertis superveniunt. Aluus quoque lubrica est reddenda, vt ante paulo docui, ne stercoris durities dolorifica fluxionem geminet: sanguis quoque malus, si abundet, corrigatur victu idoneo, & caeteris. Auertendus deinde sanguis, vt prius. Dolor leniatur oleo violato, si calor quoq; adest, vel rosato, vel amygdal. dulc. vel lini, vel lumbricorum, millepedarum, scarabeorum cum vitello ouirmi capanis cum lacte & oui vitello cocta, albumine oui tandem adiecto, et adipe gallinae

page.notes: The first word is a fragment carried over from the previous page ("fior" from "superior"?); the number and catchword are as printed. Line-end hyphens restored where printed. Possible doubtful readings: "oesypo" (oesypo), "ouirmi" (ouium?), "anastomotica" rendered as printed. Final line "adipe gallinae" continues beyond the visible text with a small mark below.
